title: Procyanidin Suppresses Tilapia Lake Virus Replication and Confers Challenge Protection in Nile Tilapia Accompanied by Modulation of Innate Antiviral Gene Expression
content:
ABSTRACT

Tilapia lake virus is a major constraint to sustainable Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) production, yet effective antiviral interventions remain limited. We evaluated the antiviral potential of procyanidin against tilapia lake virus (TiLV) using complementary cell-based and in vivo challenge models involving 300 Nile tilapia. Procyanidin displayed a concentration-dependent safety profile, with a non-cytotoxic concentration of 0.0128 mg/mL in E-11 cells and an estimated LC10 of 0.6528 mg/mL in fish. At the selected cellular concentration, procyanidin prevented virus-associated cytopathic effects and reduced TiLV RNA in culture supernatants to below the RT–qPCR detection limit. In vivo, procyanidin administration 24 h before or after viral challenge increased survival from 43.33% in untreated infected fish to 80.00% and 73.33%, respectively, corresponding to relative percent survival values of 64.44% and 52.22%. Treatment also reduced brain viral load by up to 3.12 log10 units and was associated with qualitatively better-preserved brain and liver histoarchitecture. Hepatic transcriptional profiling revealed distinct treatment-associated expression patterns across inflammatory, innate immune recognition, antigen presentation, cellular immunity and antiviral interferon signalling pathways, with pre-treatment producing the strongest induction of several antiviral genes. Together, these findings identify procyanidin as a candidate antiviral compound against tilapia lake virus, with in vitro antiviral activity accompanied in vivo by improved survival, reduced brain viral load and treatment-associated changes in hepatic immune-gene expression, although the underlying protective mechanism remains to be established.
